papers.title: Design and evaluation of an agent-based digital-twin-inspired simulation for metacognition research in higher education
papers.summary: Background There is a significant gap between sophisticated models of metacognition and empirical testing of these models in educational settings, especially the hierarchical AMERT model. Agent-based simulation frameworks, and their conceptual evolution toward simulation-based digital twins, remain largely underutilized in higher education as virtual laboratories for hypothesis generation, despite their potential to model complex developmental dynamics. Objective This study aimed to design and internally evaluate a simulation-based digital twin framework that combines the five-level AMERT model and agent-based architecture to investigate the dynamics of metacognitive development. Method Using Design and Development Research (DDR), we developed the framework through theoretical synthesis and subjected its conceptual content to expert review via a modified Delphi method with 12 experts. Student agents were simulated using NetLogo and represented four computational learner archetypes. Instructional scenarios were simulated for 150 ticks and repeated 50 times for each scenario, and internal consistency of the simulation logic was examined using Graph Neural Networks; the outputs remained systematically distinguishable across the predefined computational archetypes (89% classification accuracy). papers.title: Knowledge Graphs as External Memory for LLM-based Scientific Assistants
papers.summary: Scientific assistants must remember the questions, observations, parameters, and intermediate results that accumulate across days or weeks of inquiry, and trace each conclusion back to its evidence. Large Language Models (LLMs) lack such a structured, persistent memory, which causes contextual degradation, hallucinations, and excessive cost from overusing the context window. This thesis proposes a neuro-symbolic architecture that couples an LLM-based agent with a knowledge graph (KG) built on standardized formal languages (RDF, RDFS, OWL 2 RL, SHACL, SPARQL) and reusing existing ontologies (e.g. PROV-O) whenever possible. In contrast to state-of-the-art memory systems, which rely on schemaless or proprietary property graphs, our hypothesis is that grounding agent memory in open standards improves the six memory operations (consolidation, indexing, updating, forgetting, retrieval, compression) through formal reasoning and declarative validation, at a latency overhead that stays negligible relative to the LLM call. We present the problem, three research questions and their hypotheses, a first experimental prototype that implements an end-to-end store-and-retrieve pipeline, and an evaluation plan combining the LongMemEval and LoCoMo benchmarks with a test case in metabolomics.

papers.title: RaspAssistant as an Agentic Framework for Automating Adsorption Simulation Research in Porous Materials
papers.summary: Porous-material adsorption studies require coordinated structure preparation, force-field selection, simulation, validation, and interpretation, making end-to-end automation difficult. We test whether RaspAssistant, a hierarchical multi-agent framework, can carry an adsorption study from force-field preparation through validation and downstream separation analysis. Across twelve multi-agent workflow-reproduction runs spanning four adsorption and separation benchmarks, overall scores ranged from 8.50 to 10.00 on a rubric evaluating workflow correctness, simulation validity, and analysis consistency. In a separate eight-case force-field extraction benchmark, the mean weighted score was 0.967, combining parameter agreement and RASPA readiness. In open-ended studies, the system diagnosed and refined an acetylene force field and, after validating a CO$_2$ force field against MFI experiments, screened 197 pure-silica zeolites that passed automated input checks. These results demonstrate autonomous workflow execution after task specification and input provision: RaspAssistant coordinates, validates, adapts, and documents extended adsorption-simulation workflows while exposing model sensitivity and methodological limitations for expert review.

papers.title: Automated Multi-Agent Organization Design: From Architecture Search to Organizational Learning
papers.summary: Agentic system design is increasingly shifting from hand-crafted prompts and workflows toward automated search over agentic programs and interaction structures, with multi-agent systems receiving growing attention. Yet a central question remains unresolved: when does an automatically generated multi-agent structure exhibit a functionally meaningful division of responsibility? We argue that automated multi-agent design should move beyond searching for effective architectures toward identifying which responsibilities are functionally necessary, how they should be allocated, and when they should change. To explore this, we propose Automated Multi-Agent Organization Design (AMOD), which treats organization itself as a first-class design object, explicitly modeling how agent teams are composed, what functional responsibilities the agents assume, how they coordinate, and how collective decisions are made. We formulate AMOD as an execution-driven design loop. For each task, an automated designer instantiates an organization by assigning functional responsibilities and coordination rules to a set of agents. After execution, task outcomes, intermediate artifacts, and interaction traces are examined to identify which responsibilities may be missing, duplicated, or ineffective, and the organization is revised accordingly. papers.title: Intelligent educational agent-based collaborative scaffolding for STEM interdisciplinary project-based learning: a multi-dimensional framework and empirical evaluation
papers.summary: STEM interdisciplinary project-based learning (PBL) asks students to knit together knowledge their courses have kept apart, and to do so while absorbing the ordinary friction of group work. Scaffolding designed for single-discipline tasks rarely keeps pace with either demand. This paper proposes an intelligent educational agent-based collaborative scaffolding model comprising four architectural layers—data perception, intelligent analysis, strategy decision, and interaction execution—supported by three specialized functional agents targeting cognitive guidance, process coordination, and reflection facilitation. A multi-dimensional feature fusion approach employing scaled dot-product attention diagnoses collaborative states in near real time, reaching a macro-averaged $$\:{F}_{1}$$ of 0.83 on a test set split by team, and a timing policy trained with Proximal Policy Optimization decides when to intervene while a fading rule decides when to withdraw. Twenty-four five-member teams (120 undergraduates) completed two interdisciplinary projects over six weeks under agent-based scaffolding, teacher-led scaffolding, or unsupported collaboration. Because students were nested in teams and several outcomes are defined at team level, condition effects were estimated with baseline-adjusted, cluster-robust models rather than treating the 120 students as independent. papers.title: A PRIVACY PRESERVING PERSONAL AI ASSISTANT AND THE COST OF CLOUD MODEL INFERENCE: ARCHITECTURE, CAPABILITY TRADEOFFS, AND EVALUATION PROTOCOL
papers.summary: Personal AI assistants need reliable research and controlled access to private data. This report specifies a local-first Windows architecture and examines the capability, privacy, and operating-cost tradeoff between local Llama 3.2 3B through Ollama and self-hosted Kimi K2.5 on rented NVIDIA GPUs. We analyzed a supplied project design summary, mapped trust boundaries and failure modes, and calculated illustrative costs from a documented eight-H200 deployment and published rental rates. The design separates public research from authenticated browser sessions, enforces permissions outside the model, and requires evidence-supported answers. At an illustrative $4.59 per GPU-hour, eight H200s cost $36.72 per running hour, $4,406.40 for four hours daily over 30 days, or $26,438.40 for continuous 30-day operation, before storage and operations. An assumed 100 W incremental local draw for four hours daily at $0.15/kWh costs $1.80 monthly on an existing PC. These are scenarios, not measured deployments. Kimi K2.5 offers multimodal and agentic capabilities that a text-only 3B baseline should not be assumed to match; no matched end-to-end test was performed. Stronger cloud inference can impose substantial dedicated GPU rental cost and transfers prompts to a cloud operator. papers.title: SAGE-HAP: Sustainability-Certified Agentic Communication and Computing at a Solar-Powered High-Altitude Platform
papers.summary: The solar-powered High-Altitude Platforms (HAP) can provide persistent communication and computing services beyond terrestrial coverage. However, changing mission priorities, coupled resource demands, and uncertain solar supply complicate sustainable scheduling, while large language model proposals require independent feasibility checks. This paper proposes SAGE, a Sustainability-certified Agentic Ground-service Engine for a HAP. We formulate an energy-causal stochastic optimization problem incorporating semantic modes, multi-user interference, channel aging, essential platform loads, and battery stress. An agent translates operator intent into typed admission, mode, and grouping candidates, while deterministic convex refinement and an action shield verify resource and reserve feasibility using calibrated solar lower bounds before execution. Agent proposals and deterministic fallbacks share the same certification path. Residual-based forecasting and memory-assisted replanning close the control loop. We establish fixed-candidate convexity, reserve safety under calibrated solar coverage and bounded actuation error, and an online utility bound accounting for candidate-generation error. At nominal load, simulations show 2.38 percentage points higher completion and 5.27% greater useful-workload energy efficiency than energy-harvesting Lyapunov control. Under stressed load and solar

papers.title: Graduated Autonomy for Artificial Intelligence Agents in Human Capital Management: A Systematic Review and a Consequence-Calibrated Governance Framework
papers.summary: Human capital management platforms are starting to embed software agents built on large language models. Unlike earlier analytics tools, these agents can plan a sequence of steps, call system functions and change employee records. Artificial intelligence is therefore moving from advising managers to acting for them. Most governance guidance, however, was written for systems that recommend rather than act. This study asks how organisations should match the autonomy of such agents to the consequences of the people decisions they touch. A systematic review was conducted and reported using the PRISMA 2020 guideline. Eighteen structured searches of a multi-source scholarly index returned 180 records. After duplicate removal and eligibility screening, 55 peer-reviewed sources were retained, and four foundational and regulatory sources were added. Thematic synthesis produced seven findings. Algorithmic control of work is already extensive. Bias in hiring tools is persistent and partly organisational. Human review is weaker than assumed, because reviewers often defer to machine advice. Responsibility tends to diffuse as systems gain autonomy. Employee trust depends on fair process and visible human involvement. Language-model agents add new failure modes, such as fabricated content and hidden instructions planted in documents. Finally, current governance frameworks rarely specify contr

papers.title: Design and Evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence–Based Model for Predicting Twelfth-Grade Students’ Mathematics Performance Based on Individual, Educational, and Learning Technology Factors
papers.summary: Purpose: This study aimed to design and evaluate an artificial intelligence–based model for predicting the mathematics performance of twelfth-grade experimental sciences students based on individual, educational, and learning technology factors. Methods and Materials: This applied, quantitative, cross-sectional, and predictive study was conducted among twelfth-grade experimental sciences students in Isfahan, Iran. A total of 187 questionnaires were distributed, and after removing incomplete, inconsistent, and invalid records, data from 84 students were retained for analysis. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire assessing individual factors, educational conditions, and learning technology variables, together with students’ recorded mathematics scores. The dataset was divided into training and testing subsets, and repeated five-fold cross-validation was used for internal model development. Multiple linear regression, ridge regression, lasso regression, elastic net regression, decision tree regression, random forest regression, gradient boosting regression, and support vector regression were compared. Model performance was evaluated using mean absolute error, root mean squared error, and the coefficient of determination. papers.title: Neuro-Symbolic Meta-policies for Temporal Knowledge-Graph Memory Under Partial Observability
Perceptions and recommendations: exploring the ethics of using satellite data to understand, monitor, and publish research on international geohazards
papers.summary: Abstract. Over the last ten years, open-access earth observation satellite data volumes have grown exponentially. Through use of this data, geohazard remote sensing scientists' abilities to impact policy and reduce societal vulnerability to geohazards has become increasingly tangible. However, much of this open-access data is acquired, stored, and disseminated by the Global North, whilst most disasters take place in the Global South. Furthermore, many societies are imaged by these earth observation satellites perhaps without knowing these satellites exist. There exists little ethical guidance for remote sensing researchers in navigating ethical risks that may arise during geohazard research which uses satellite data. We explore these ethical considerations with UK based geohazard remote sensing scientists through thirteen interviews and three focus group discussions. We discuss with scientists their thoughts on ethical review systems for geohazard remote sensing; the importance of visiting study regions; how data should be handled which images people and societies; the desired impact these scientists want to achieve; and the ethical risks of open data. We find among remote sensing researchers in industry, government organisations, and academia a deep desire to contribute to the reduction of societal vulnerabilities to geohazards. papers.title: BEYOND TECHNOSTRESS AI Fatigue as a Cumulative Adaptation Burden in Education and Work
papers.summary: Artificial intelligence has become a persistent layer of work and learning rather than an occasional tool. Users must repeatedly decide when to delegate, how to prompt, whether to trust, how to verify, and how responsibility should be distributed. This integrative review defines AI fatigue as a cumulative reduction in the cognitive, affective, or motivational capacity for adaptive AI engagement when interaction, evaluation, correction, learning, and role-adjustment demands accumulate faster than recovery and support. The review connects technostress, automation vigilance, cognitive load and offloading, trust calibration, digital fatigue, and the Job Demands–Resources perspective. It introduces an Exposure–Adaptation–Depletion–Response framework, a five-domain taxonomy, and an AI Fatigue Load model that separates use volume from uncertainty, task stakes, correction burden, interruption, role disruption, and imposed adoption velocity. The analysis is updated to incorporate a 2026 validated 15-item AI Fatigue Scale; the proposed load model complements that psychophysiological outcome measure by specifying socio-technical antecedents and exposure conditions. Educational and organizational applications show why AI may simultaneously improve output and worsen human sustainability. The article identifies recurring inferential errors, presents a measurement and longitudinal research ag

papers.title: TME LLM OS: A Closed-Loop Systems Engineering Architecture for Epistemic Correction in AI Agent Systems Systems Engineering Proposal
From Artificial Intelligence to Institutional Intelligence
papers.summary: Generative artificial intelligence and agentic systems can redistribute reading, research, synthesis, criticism, drafting, and coordination within courts. This article asks how that redistribution changes judicial cognition and which institutional safeguards are needed to preserve legitimate adjudication. Through an interdisciplinary narrative review and doctrinal analysis, it develops a framework of institutional intelligence anchored in Brazilian National Council of Justice Resolution No. 615/2025, as amended by Resolution No. 674/2026. Five categories organize the argument: institutional cognitive space describes the allocation of cognitive work; artificial adversariality identifies structured internal challenge among agents; the institutional rein integrates controls over delegated autonomy; meaningful human initiative emphasizes the continuing human authority to frame problems and determine purposes; and institutional AI curation describes the competence required to select, validate, contextualize, and reject artificial contributions. Recent research on human–AI collaboration and multi-agent failure qualifies the framework: neither human review nor artificial disagreement guarantees reliability, and short-term performance gains do not establish long-term professional competence. The article distinguishes technical auditability from legal reason-giving and internal agent de

papers.title: Evolving Agent Interfaces
papers.summary: Computer-use agents are limited by the interfaces humans give them. An agent may type a spreadsheet cell by cell when a single line of code would do, or print all two thousand lines of a file through a shell to find one function. Both the interfaces and the knowledge of when to use each are built by hand, which cannot keep pace with new applications, workflows, and models. We argue that interface design should itself be an agent capability. We introduce Agent S4, an autonomous computer-use scientist that builds Evolving Agent Interfaces from task experience. A meta-agent examines task agents' trajectories on synthetic training tasks, without success labels, and constructs and revises interfaces and usage knowledge in a repository. Population-based evolution then selects which repositories to develop further by their performance on validation tasks the meta-agent never sees, favoring changes that generalize beyond the seen tasks. On OSWorld V2, Agent S4, with Qwen3.8-27B and the evolved repository of interfaces, sets a new state of the art in open-source computer-use agents, reaching 21.3% binary score, 3.8 times the same model with fixed interfaces. This is above both GPT-5.5 (13.0%) and Claude Opus 4.8 (20.6%), at about 4.3% and 1.5% of their respective costs. On ScienceBoard, the evolved interfaces improve the success rate from 41.4% to 58.6% with the same model. These result

papers.title: InterWebCoder: Learning Interactive Webpage Generation from Executable Tests via Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Interactive webpages underpin modern applications, but reproducing both their visual appearance and multi-step behavior remains challenging for multimodal large language models (MLLMs). Scalable training data must capture user actions, state transitions, and expected outcomes, while real-world webpage code is often entangled with irrelevant scripts and external dependencies. Moreover, existing GUI-agent-based verification provides slow and potentially unstable functional feedback. To address these challenges, we propose InterWebCoder, an efficient framework for interactive webpage code generation. InterWebCoder introduces a Test-Specification-Guided and Execution-Verified Data Synthesis pipeline that records real-world interaction trajectories and synthesizes self-contained webpage code with executable test scripts. A failureattributed repair mechanism uses runtime evidence to locate and iteratively fix errors in either the webpage code or test script. We then combine test-ID-weighted supervised fine-tuning with group-relative policy optimization, directly optimizing functional correctness and visual fidelity using test pass rates and state-level visual similarity. This replaces costly GUI-agent verification with fast, reproducible executable feedback. Our pipeline produces 1,736 verified samples from 2,058 tasks, achieving an 84.35% synthesis success rate. papers.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
papers.summary: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-perf

papers.title: Exploring or Exploiting Generative AI? A Dual-Path, Dual-Horizon Theory of Employee Incremental and Radical Creativity
papers.summary: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. This article therefore does not present the basic dual path as a new discovery. Instead, it develops a theoretical integration and dynamic extension that asks why the established paths operate differently, when employees should switch between them, and how short-run augmentation can evolve into either capability accumulation or capability substitution. We distinguish expansive and consolidative modes of knowledge integration, theorize phase-congruent switching rather than static ``high-high'' ambidexterity, and position metacognition as a control mechanism that governs both immediate knowledge conversion and longer-run cognitive development. We further specify cultural tightness and psychological safety as directional boundary conditions and distinguish individual creative gains from collective idea-space diversity. The framework converts emerging empirical regularities into falsifiable propositions about task phase, context, and time, providing a research agenda for sustainable human--AI creativity.

papers.title: Helping the Helper: LLM-Assisted Problem Articulation for Older Adults Seeking Technology Support
papers.summary: Older adults often struggle to articulate technology support needs due to unfamiliar technical terminology and age-related cognitive changes. We explore how large language models (LLMs) can facilitate this problem articulation process. Through a diary study (n = 27), we identified four communication barriers in older adults’ queries: verbosity, incompleteness, over-specification, and under-specification. To mitigate these, we developed an LLM pipeline that clarifies context and paraphrases unstructured queries. LLM-rephrased queries significantly improved automated solution accuracy (69% vs. 35%). Furthermore, younger adults (n = 48) acting as technology helpers understood LLM-rephrased queries better (93.7% vs. 65.8%) and reported greater ease in providing support. Older adults (n = 34) also found the resulting solutions highly actionable (94.7%). Finally, we contribute the first synthetic dataset of older adults’ technology assistance queries (STAQ). This work demonstrates how LLMs can improve technology support seeking for older adults by addressing age-related communication barriers.

papers.title: Important roles of AKAP150-anchored PKA and CaN in mediating crosstalk between LTP and LTD and consequently LTP/LTD balance
papers.summary: Long-term potentiation (LTP) and long-term depression (LTD) at hippocampal CA1 glutamatergic synapses are opposing forms of synaptic plasticity that support learning and memory. Their expression depends on coordinated kinase and phosphatase signaling that regulates AMPA receptor (AMPAR) trafficking, yet mechanisms that couple LTP and LTD and maintain their balance remain incompletely understood. AKAP150 is a postsynaptic scaffold that anchors protein kinase A (PKA), which promotes AMPAR phosphorylation and potentiation, and calcineurin (CaN), which promotes AMPAR dephosphorylation and depression. We hypothesized that AKAP150 coordinates crosstalk between these pathways. We developed interference peptides targeting the PKA- and CaN-binding regions of AKAP150 and validated their ability to disrupt the respective interactions and associated enzymatic activities. Using hippocampal slice and in vivo electrophysiology, we examined decaying LTP induced by a weak high-frequency stimulation protocol, non-decaying LTP induced by stronger stimulation, and LTD induced by prolonged low frequency stimulation. Disrupting AKAP150-CaN converted decaying LTP into sustained LTP and prevented LTD without affecting non-decaying LTP. Disrupting AKAP150-PKA prevented both decaying and non-decaying LTP and partially reduced LTD. Behavioral experiments further showed that altering these interactions mo

papers.title: Career transition as an assemblage of learning : a multiple case study of Korean millennials who left socially desirable workplaces
papers.summary: In this dissertation, I examine the career transitions of Korean millennials who left socially desirable workplaces. I problematize understandings of career transition as merely an individual choice, a matter of personal motivation, or a response to structural change. I also use the term millennials critically, not as a fixed or homogeneous generational category, but as a situated and contested designation that helps locate participants’ biographies and experiences within particular social, historical, educational, and labour-market conditions. I developed the conceptual framework of career transition as an assemblage of learning, drawing on Billett’s concept of the personal curriculum, Kang et al.’s learning management apparatus, and Deleuze and Guattari’s assemblage thinking. I designed the research as a qualitative multiple case study to examine each participant’s career transition holistically. Data were generated through biographical interviews incorporating image-elicitation and life-mapping activities, walking interviews, and digital ethnographic engagement. The findings show that leaving socially desirable positions was not an isolated individual decision, but emerged within and through existing social and material relations. Participants questioned and revisited established pathways, experimented with side-work opportunities through social ties, engaged with platform-m

papers.title: FARABI: fuzzy-assisted routing for adaptive blockage-resilient 6G IoV
papers.summary: High-frequency millimeter-wave (mmWave) and Terahertz (THz) communications are promising for 6G Internet of Vehicles (IoV) services but remain vulnerable to dynamic vehicular mobility, bursty heterogeneous traffic, and heavy-tailed physical blockage. Conventional routing approaches often rely on memoryless channel models, non-differentiable soft-computing heuristics, or centralized optimization that may not adequately capture blockage persistence and tail-latency risks. This paper presents FARABI (Fuzzy-Assisted Routing for Adaptive Blockage-Resilient 6G IoV), a cross-layer Software-Defined Networking (SDN) routing framework that integrates a three-state semi-Markov blockage model, multi-class Markov-Modulated Poisson Process (MMPP) traffic, a seven-dimensional differentiable fuzzy inference system, and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR)-based risk-aware routing optimization. The framework tracks blockage age to estimate residual interruption duration and incorporates queueing, link reliability, route sustainability, and traffic-class requirements into an online hierarchical primal-dual optimization process. Extensive simulation-based evaluation under dynamic blockage, mobility, and bursty traffic conditions shows that the FARABI control-plane execution time increases from 0.5 ms to 1.85 ms as the decision space grows from 450 to 18,000 variables, corresponding to up to 42.08× lo

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence as a Catalyst for Sustainable Development and Business Transformation: A Conceptual Study
papers.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly positioned at the intersection of business transformation and sustainable development. Its capacity to identify patterns in large datasets, forecast demand and risk, automate routine processes, support product innovation, and improve resource allocation creates opportunities to enhance organizational performance while addressing environmental and social priorities. Yet these outcomes are not automatic: AI can reproduce bias, intensify surveillance, displace or transform work, widen digital inequalities, and consume substantial energy and material resources. This conceptual study synthesizes the supplied literature review on AI-enabled sustainability, digital transformation, innovation, governance, and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). It develops an integrated framework in which AI capabilities influence sustainable business transformation through three complementary mechanisms: operational and resource optimization, innovation capability, and data-driven decision-making. The proposed framework links AI adoption with economic, environmental, and social sustainability through digital infrastructure, workforce skills, organizational readiness, and collaboration. Responsible governance, fairness, accountability, and data protection ensure ethical implementation. AI-driven sustainability requires strategic alignment, organization

papers.title: SHAPING SELF-REGULATED AND METACOGNITIVE LEARNING THROUGH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND LEARNING ANALYTICS
papers.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) and learning analytics are increasingly embedded in educational systems, yet their implications for self-regulated learning (SRL) and metacognitive development remain only partially understood. This study conducts a systematic literature review of 34 empirical and review articles investigating AI-driven learning analytics in formal education settings, focusing on their impact on SRL, motivation, and academic performance. Following PRISMA-aligned procedures, the review identifies studies involving AI-based analytics tools, standardized SRL or metacognitive assessments, and empirical designs with pre–post or comparison data. The results indicate that AI-driven systems such as predictive models, adaptive platforms, chatbots, and generative AI can strengthen core SRL processes, increase motivation and engagement, and improve academic outcomes across diverse subjects and educational levels. However, the review also reveals persistent implementation challenges, including infrastructural limitations, teacher preparedness, privacy and ethical issues, and potential over-reliance on AI that may weaken independent strategic thinking. The article concludes that AI-driven learning analytics can meaningfully support SRL when embedded within coherent pedagogical frameworks and supported by institutional policies, and it outlines directions for future research on m

papers.title: The new constructionism. Papert after Peirce: indexicality, navigational thinking, and learning in the age of generative AI
papers.summary: The arrival of generative AI in every classroom has produced a crisis that is at once technological, epistemological, and pedagogical. We argue that the appropriate response is neither prohibition nor naive adoption, but a principled reconstruction of constructionism for a computational environment that is generative, context-sensitive, and dialogically accessible. Drawing on Peircean semiotics, Papertian constructionism, Polanyi's epistemology, and contemporary neural-network research, we develop a programmatic framework we call the New Constructionism. We make four connected contributions. First, we argue that generative AI introduces an indexical mode of computation: its relation to the empirical world may be direct, mediated, or incomplete, but in a situated human–AI configuration meaning is operationally conditioned by conversational history, artifacts, tools, observations, and action. Second, we introduce a three-dimensional analytical space — semiotic, psycho-epistemological, and pedagogical — in which learning paradigms can be located and compared. Third, we reinterpret the history of programming education as a movement from a predominantly symbolic environment toward a hybrid ecology in which symbolic execution, distributional generation, and situated reference coexist. This hybridity qualifies but does not cancel the indexical turn at the level of interaction and educ

papers.title: Video and digital games: Historical controversies, benefits, and risks for children and adolescents
papers.summary: Video and digital games have been the focus of sustained public and scientific debate since their commercial emergence in the late 1970s, particularly regarding their effects on children and adolescents. Early public and scientific discourse frequently portrayed gaming as a source of physical injury, addiction, aggression, social isolation, academic problems, and moral decline. However, subsequent empirical research has produced a substantially more differentiated picture of both the benefits and risks of gaming. This review examines the historical foundations of controversies surrounding video and digital games and synthesizes contemporary evidence concerning their cognitive, emotional, social, therapeutic, and physical effects. . Research indicates that moderate, purposeful gaming may improve visuospatial abilities, attentional control, problem-solving, mood regulation, social connection, and selected educational outcomes. Gaming-based interventions have also demonstrated therapeutic potential, particularly for depressive symptoms and attention-related difficulties among young people. At the same time, important risks remain, especially when gaming becomes excessive, compulsive, or disruptive to everyday functioning. These include repetitive-strain injuries, sleep disruption, problematic gaming, and adverse mental-health and academic outcomes. Evidence concerning violent game

papers.title: Mapping The Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Group Creative Processes: A Scoping Review
papers.summary: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is finding its way into creative work at a growing pace, yet its specific role within collaborative creative processes, those involving multiple people working together, remains poorly understood and fragmented across the literature. This scoping review maps the empirical research on integrating GenAI into group creative processes, outlining creative domains, tasks, AI tools, AI roles, stages of integration, and reported outcomes. Following PRISMA-ScR and JBI guidance, a systematic search was conducted across Scopus, Web of Science, and PsycINFO. Empirical peer-reviewed studies were included when they involved at least two human participants engaged in a collaborative creative process supported by GenAI. Thirty-eight studies met the inclusion criteria. The majority were conducted in educational and design contexts, with brainstorming, content creation, and design development emerging as the most frequent task types. GenAI was most often integrated as a co-creative partner, typically during the ideation stage or across multiple phases of the creative process. Reported benefits included enhanced ideation, greater efficiency, improved engagement, and stronger collaboration quality, while the main tensions revolved around over-reliance on AI, cognitive offloading, homogenization of ideas, and unresolved questions of authorship and

papers.title: CARRS: A Constraint-Aware, Real-Time Routing System for Emergency Vehicles in Urban Environments
papers.summary: Emergency vehicles such as police vehicles, fire engines, and ambulances require a stable and efficient route optimization to reach life-critical events in the shortest times possible. However, the dynamic nature of urban traffic makes this ideal scenario much more challenging, causing critical life-threatening delays. Traditional civilian navigation systems cannot account for real-time traffic changes alongside vehicle-specific constraints, creating inadequate routing scenarios. This research presents the Constraint-Aware Real-Time Routing System (CARRS), a unified software architecture tailored for emergency coordination. The CARRS architecture is engineered to fuse together classical pathfinding algorithms such as A*, Dijkstra, and Bidirectional A*, with Constraint Satisfaction Problem methodologies. The Design Science Research Methodology is the research framework, and prototyping is the iterative process. The artifact was empirically evaluated using OpenStreetMap data for major metropolitan road networks, combined with simulated dynamic traffic scenarios. Performance metrics focused on route optimality, constraint adherence, rerouting responsiveness, and the potential for future system scalability. Findings revealed the system's capability to generate optimal routes for operationally relevant subgraphs in under 35 seconds, with incremental rerouting responsiveness below 20

papers.title: Adoption of Automation and Smart Technologies in Modern Textile Production Systems
papers.summary: Automation, artificial intelligence, connected sensing technologies, digital twins, robotics, and data-driven control systems are increasingly transforming textile and apparel production systems. However, in existing studies, these technologies have often been analyzed separately or limited to specific factories, countries, or specific stages of the production process. The study created an integrated analytical framework for analyzing the maturity of technology adoption in modern textile production systems, with a new dataset based on data collected from various sources related to technology adoption and digital readiness open to the public. The complete dataset contains a total of 8,198 analytical observations and 26 variables. The dataset covers nine manufacturing and business activities for the period 2019-2023 in five countries - Bangladesh, Chile, Ethiopia, India and Senegal. As part of this study, a subset of 5,472 production-based observations were used for predictive modeling. This subset is divided into 3,830 trainings, 821 validations, and 821 test observations, respectively, in a group-conscious manner. The study compared the performance of four models: Random Forest, XGBoost, Support Vector Machine and One-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (1D CNN). papers.title: Q&A or Document-Based? The Effects of Interface Type on How Screen Reader Users Access Interconnected Documents
papers.summary: Blind and low-vision (BLV) users are increasingly engaging with large language model (LLM) interfaces to access documents, but it is unclear how such systems support or hinder their ability to build interconnected knowledge. To examine this gap, we compared a Question-Answer Interface (QAI) that supports open-ended conversational inquiry, with a Document Interface (DI) based mostly on traditional structured text document navigation. We recruited 16 BLV screen reader users where they used both interfaces to explore two fictional worlds. Data from interaction logs, concept maps, decision-based tasks, and semi-structured interviews provide comparative insights into how interface design supports knowledge construction. Findings show that participants visited more distinct documents with the DI and formed larger and more correct mental models with the DI than with the QAI. They were also more able to apply knowledge they had gained. Simultaneously, many still preferred the QAI and often estimated that they had explored more, formed better mental models and applied their models better when acquiring the information with the QAI, despite this not being the case. Our analysis suggests possible interface design reasons for these differences and highlights some of the risks introduced by using question-answer interfaces to access information spaces.
